title: Workflow Composer Checkpoint C and save/reopen walkthrough
summary: The local engineer created the bounded four-block graphical draft, verified text/canvas parity, saved revision 2, closed it, and reopened identical semantic and layout identities without browser diagnostics.

manualSteps.label: Create draft
manualSteps.instruction: Open **Workflow Composer**, review the draft boundary, and click **Create working draft**.

manualSteps.label: Add blocks
manualSteps.instruction: Click **Capture input**, **Engineering work**, **Review**, and **Release boundary** in order.

manualSteps.label: Inspect composition
manualSteps.instruction: Compare **First-party diagram** and **Canonical text projection**, then select **Define product**.

manualSteps.label: Close and reopen
manualSteps.instruction: Click **Close**, then click **Reopen saved draft** and compare revision and identity digests.

steps.label: Create a separate empty draft
steps.summary: The normal UI created revision 1 without changing the released Process Definition.
steps.purpose: Begin from the supported empty-draft boundary.
steps.action: Kept the visible title and purpose values and clicked Create working draft.
steps.value: Product definition draft; Capture, define, review, and release one product definition.
steps.expected: A feature-bounded working draft opens at revision 1 with no released or executable authority.
steps.actual: Revision 1 opened with the Working draft and Not released · Not executable labels.

steps.label: Add Capture requirements
steps.summary: Capture requirements entered the canonical draft and both projections.
steps.purpose: Advance the bounded representative workflow without inventing renderer-owned identities.
steps.expected: Capture requirements appears in the diagram and text projection with its stable host-owned identities.
steps.actual: Capture requirements appeared and the next bounded palette action became available.

steps.label: Add Define product
steps.summary: Define product entered the canonical draft and both projections.
steps.purpose: Advance the bounded representative workflow without inventing renderer-owned identities.
steps.expected: Define product appears in the diagram and text projection with its stable host-owned identities.
steps.actual: Define product appeared and the next bounded palette action became available.

steps.label: Add Review product definition
steps.summary: Review product definition entered the canonical draft and both projections.
steps.purpose: Advance the bounded representative workflow without inventing renderer-owned identities.
steps.expected: Review product definition appears in the diagram and text projection with its stable host-owned identities.
steps.actual: Review product definition appeared and the next bounded palette action became available.

steps.label: Add Release product definition
steps.summary: Release product definition entered the canonical draft and both projections.
steps.purpose: Advance the bounded representative workflow without inventing renderer-owned identities.
steps.expected: Release product definition appears in the diagram and text projection with its stable host-owned identities.
steps.actual: Release product definition appeared and the next bounded palette action became available.

steps.label: Compare the complete graphical and text composition
steps.summary: Diagram and text expose the same 23 unique semantic identities and complete declared workflow relationships.
steps.purpose: Prove the first reviewable graphical slice uses one canonical model.
steps.action: Compared the complete diagram and text semantic identity sets.
steps.expected: Both projections contain exactly the same 23 unique semantic identities.
steps.actual: Both identity sets matched exactly at 23, including phases, blocks, ports, connections, gate, feedback, and intended artifacts.

steps.label: Select and inspect one semantic block
steps.summary: Canvas selection and inspector identity agree without changing draft bytes.
steps.purpose: Prove host-owned selection across the renderer seam.
steps.action: Clicked Define product in the diagram.
steps.expected: The block exposes a non-color selected state and the inspector shows block.define-product.
steps.actual: The button exposed aria-pressed=true, visible Selected text, and the inspector showed the same stable ID.

steps.label: Validate the complete draft
steps.summary: Server validation accepted the bounded semantic and layout candidate.
steps.purpose: Verify all references and saved layout are valid before persistence.
steps.expected: Validation passes and the inspector does not show contradictory diagnostics.
steps.actual: The status and inspector consistently reported validation passed.

steps.label: Save revision 2 atomically
steps.summary: The valid four-block candidate saved as revision 2 with semantic and layout identities visible.
steps.purpose: Prove the normal guarded save path.
steps.expected: The server advances to revision 2 and reports both identity digests.
steps.actual: Revision 2 appeared and both semantic and layout digests remained visible.

steps.label: Close the editor session
steps.summary: The editor closed while retaining the saved revision and both identity digests.
steps.purpose: Separate browser working-session state from persisted draft state.
steps.expected: The graphical editor closes and saved revision 2 remains available to reopen.
steps.actual: The closed state showed revision 2, draft ID, semantic digest, layout digest, and Reopen saved draft.

steps.label: Reopen identical semantic and layout state
steps.summary: Revision 2 reopened with identical digests, 23 canvas identities, and all four saved positions.
steps.purpose: Provide initial Checkpoint E save/reopen evidence.
steps.action: Clicked Reopen saved draft and compared saved identities and positions.
steps.expected: Revision, semantic digest, layout digest, 23 identities, and four positions match the saved state.
steps.actual: Revision 2 reopened with identical digests, 23 identities, and four saved position records.
